draft.title: Levels of organisation
card: Cells in a multicellular organism are specialised. Each type has a structure that suits its job.
Tissue
a group of similar cells that work together to do one job, such as muscle tissue.
Organ
a structure made of several different tissues that work together, such as the stomach.
System
a group of organs that work together to carry out a major body function, such as the digestive system.
draft.remember: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, and organs make systems.

a.q: Which of these is an example of an organ?
opts: The heart, made of muscle, nerve and connective tissue
Cardiac muscle cells that contract together
A single red blood cell
The circulatory system
a.why: The heart is made of several different tissues that work together. Cardiac muscle alone is one tissue, and the circulatory system is a group of organs, so it is a system.
a.clue: Look for the one made of several different tissues.

b.q: A leaf contains epidermis, palisade tissue and xylem, which together carry out photosynthesis. At which level of organisation is the leaf?
opts: Organ, as it is made of several tissues working together
Tissue, as it is made of similar cells doing one job
System, as it carries out a major function
Cell, as it is the smallest unit of a plant
b.why: The leaf is made of different tissues that work together, so it is an organ. It is not a tissue, because its cells are not all of one type. It is not a system, because it is a single structure and not a group of organs.
b.clue: Count how many different tissues are in the leaf.

a.best: The heart, made of muscle, nerve and connective tissue

b.best: Organ, as it is made of several tissues working together

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and the only one that lists precise detail (three named tissues). The clue, 'Look for the one made of several different tissues', then points straight at it, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea. Shorten it to 'The heart' or add similar detail to the other options.
